title: Exact-boundary padded verifier characterization
statement: Let $C,c\in\mathbb{N}$, let $V$ be a language of binary strings, and let $x,v$ be binary strings with $|v|=(C+1)(|x|+1)^c$. Then $xv$ belongs to the padded verifier for $C,c,V$ if and only if there is a binary string $u$ such that stripping the certificate from $v$ yields $u$, $|u|\le C(|x|+1)^c$, and the self-delimiting pair encoding of $x$ and $u$ belongs to $V$.
hypotheses_covered: $V$ is a language of binary strings
replaced:
Let $C, c \in \mathbb{N}$ and $V \subseteq \{0,1\}^{*}$, and let
$V^{\mathrm{pad}}_{C,c}$ be the set of binary strings $y$ such that, for the least
$n$ with $n + (C+1)(n+1)^c = |y|$ (which must exist), the suffix $v$ of $y$ after
its first $n$ bits contains a $1$, and the prefix $u$ of $v$ preceding its last
$1$ satisfies $|u| \le C(n+1)^c$ and $\langle x, u\rangle \in V$, where $x$ is
the first $n$ bits of $y$ and $\langle x, u\rangle$ is the self-delimiting pair
encoding ($x$ with every bit doubled, then $01$, then $u$). Then for all binary
strings $x$ and $v$ with $|v| = (C+1)(|x|+1)^c$, the concatenation $xv$ lies in
$V^{\mathrm{pad}}_{C,c}$ if and only if $v$ contains a $1$ and the prefix $u$ of
$v$ preceding its last $1$ satisfies $|u| \le C(|x|+1)^c$ and
$\langle x, u\rangle \in V$.
